paperName: The National Economy in a Global Context

questions.questionText: Changes in real GDP are used to measure

options.text: inflation.
the level of employment.
economic growth.
the distribution of income.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows two aggregate demand curves (AD) for an economy. All other things being equal, the most likely cause of the shift from AD1 to AD2 is an increase in

options.text: exports.
the rate of inflation.
interest rates.
the budget deficit.

extractionNotes: the question prints a diagram or chart (an image)
2 subscript or superscript glyph(s) set flush against their base

questions.questionText: All other things being equal, the long-run aggregate supply curve of an economy is likely to shift to the right if there is an increase in

options.text: factor mobility.
raw material prices.
indirect taxation.
wage rates.

questions.questionText: A country has a slow rate of growth of productivity and rising cyclical unemployment. All other things being equal, which measures are most likely to increase the rate of growth of productivity and reduce cyclical unemployment?

options.text: Increased investment and increased saving
More government spending on training and a higher exchange rate
Decreased benefit payments and a lower budget deficit
Lower taxation on firms and lower interest rates

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows two aggregate demand curves (AD) and the short-run aggregate supply curve (SRAS) for an economy. All other things being equal, which one of the following is the most likely cause of the movement of the economy from equilibrium at Y1 to equilibrium at Y2?

options.text: A decrease in imports
An increase in savings
A decrease in the money supply
An increase in productivity

extractionNotes: the question prints a diagram or chart (an image)
2 subscript or superscript glyph(s) set flush against their base

questions.questionText: The table below shows how the index of GDP and the index of population changed in an economy between 2011 and 2015. Which one of the following can be inferred from the data?

options.text: Population was higher than GDP in 2011
Between 2011 and 2013, GDP grew by 8% whereas population grew by 3%
There was no growth in GDP per capita between 2013 and 2015
Money GDP increased by more than real GDP between 2011 and 2015

questions.questionText: As a consequence of a severe global recession, an economy has experienced a demand-side shock and is now growing below its trend rate. All other things being equal, which one of the following combinations, A, B, C or D, is now most likely to exist in this economy?

questions.questionText: In which one of the following situations could the UK be said to be experiencing a negative output gap?

options.text: Output per worker is lower in the UK than in the USA
Real GDP in the UK is less than the economy’s productive potential
UK firms do not have sufficient productive capacity to satisfy customer demand
The skills possessed by UK workers do not match those which are required by UK employers

questions.questionText: Structural unemployment is most likely to occur because of

options.text: labour being temporarily unemployed when moving between jobs.
fluctuations in the level of aggregate demand.
the seasonal nature of certain occupations.
long-term changes in the pattern of demand for the products of particular industries.

questions.questionText: An economy is in macroeconomic equilibrium, producing at its normal capacity level of output. Without long-run economic growth, a persistent increase in aggregate demand is likely to lead to an increase in the level of

options.text: real GDP.
employment.
productivity.
prices.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following combinations, A, B, C or D, is most likely to occur in the recovery phase of the economic cycle?

questions.questionText: The current account of the balance of payments is in surplus. However, there are deficits on the balance of trade in goods and the balance of trade in services. It can be concluded that

options.text: the trade figures must be inaccurate.
the primary income (income flows) balance must be positive.
the combined primary and secondary income (income flows and transfers) balance must be positive.
the value of services exported must exceed the value of goods imported.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of contractionary fiscal policy?

options.text: Decreasing the supply of credit
Increasing spending on welfare benefits
Reducing progressive taxation
Increasing the size of the budget surplus

questions.questionText: All other things being equal, an increase in the exchange rate of the pound against other currencies due to a rise in interest rates is most likely to cause an increase in the UK’s

options.text: surplus on the current account of the balance of payments.
price of imported goods.
level of unemployment.
rate of economic growth.

questions.questionText: A budget deficit is most likely to occur when

options.text: the value of imports exceeds the value of exports.
government spending exceeds tax revenue.
the volume of imports exceeds the volume of exports.
direct and indirect taxes are reduced.

questions.questionText: The table below shows the annual percentage change in real GDP for an economy between 2013 and 2016. The long-run trend rate of growth for this economy is estimated to be 2.8%. Which one of the following statements is most likely to be correct?

options.text: In 2013, the economy’s negative output gap increased.
In 2014, the amount of spare capacity in the economy increased.
In 2015, the amount of spare capacity in the economy decreased.
In 2016, the economy’s positive output gap decreased.

extractionNotes: 5 line(s) of figure or table text printed with the question are not reproduced; see the question paper

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements relating to the use of supply-side policy is correct?

options.text: Supply-side improvements in the economy can only be brought about by government policy.
Supply-side policies are intended to increase the long-run trend rate of economic growth.
Supply-side policies are designed to reduce the size of a negative output gap.
Supply-side policies ensure increased capacity utilisation in the economy.

questions.questionText: In the circular flow of income model, which one of the following equations is correct?

options.text: Income = Output = Expenditure
Income = Output = Injections
Output = Expenditure = Withdrawals
Expenditure = Income = Injections = Withdrawals.
